task.title: Rearm exact recovery after a failed recovered-packet drain

scope.owned_layer: Assistant dev bridge exact failed-packet recovery rearm state machine, durable retry evidence chain, existing drain CLI wording, isolated regressions, and task evidence.
scope.not_changing: No supervisor scheduling, fleet policy, canonical task-state schema, live inbox contents, manual queue/recovery edit path, runtime promotion, or downstream task dispatch.

failure_sequence: An exact signed failed packet is recovered through the governed CLI and its durable recovery record reaches queued.
The recovered pending packet is drained again and fails before assignment, producing a new exact failed receipt and returning the leaf to failed storage.
The prior implementation rejects the resulting failed leaf because the durable recovery record is already queued, leaving no supported retry path.
incident.repair_boundary: The same exact-id recovery command may rearm only when packet signature/provenance, queue and dispatch fences, recovery history, and a new exact failed receipt all validate. Operators still do not edit or move inbox state manually.

delivered_properties: A queued recovery record plus an exact newly failed drain receipt now enters a supported rearm path and returns the same signed leaf to pending without draining it implicitly.

Each rearm appends a six-digit attempt record under recovery-rearms/<packet-id>/ that binds the previous recovery, the current failed receipt, the next recovery, canonical SHA-256 digests, packet identity, source/target paths, and timestamps.

The chain validates every prior attempt in order and rejects missing, stale, malformed, symlinked, ambiguous, digest-mismatched, identity-mismatched, or state-mismatched evidence before moving a leaf.
The previously consumed failed receipt digest cannot authorize another move, so manually bouncing the old pending leaf back to failed remains fail-closed.
A crash after evidence preparation, after failed-to-pending rename, or after next-recovery persistence can be resumed from the last prepared evidence without duplicating attempts.
Repeated genuine failures create consecutive evidence attempts; the regression proves attempts 1 and 2 compose before a successful governed drain.
The existing --recover-failed-packet-id CLI is the supported operator surface and now describes both initial recovery and rearm.

acceptance.statement: A recovered packet that fails a later drain before assignment can be rearmed through the exact-id CLI path.
Rearm remains packet-signature, receipt-digest, provenance, queue-lock, processing-fence, dispatch-fence, admission, and replay bound.
Consumed receipts, manual queue bounce, and tampered retry evidence fail closed without moving the failed leaf.
Prepared retry evidence resumes safely after a crash between leaf rename and recovery-record update.
Focused inbox and CLI regressions remain green and use pytest-temporary status roots and inboxes.
Fresh independent Codex2 exact-head review, protected merge, and owner closeout remain.
